subject: POC: Multilocale evaluation plan & recommended model pairing

Subject: POC: Multilocale evaluation plan & recommended model pairing

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo today — good conversation and clear alignment on the scope for a short POC. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we can lock timelines: 

Scope (what we propose to demo in the POC)
- Ingest and serve customer FAQs + triage flow for web chat (English + ES/PT/FR).
- Evaluate quality on intent accuracy and answer utility using your prompt set.
- Measure latency and per-token cost under a realistic concurrency shape (peak ~8 rps).

Success criteria (please confirm/adjust):
- Intent classification accuracy >= 88% on your test suite across languages.
- Median server-side generation latency < 300ms for EN, < 350ms for ES/PT/FR.
- 95th percentile latency <= 700ms.
- Token cost target <= $0.0025 per generated token (goal).

Timeline
- Week 0: Kickoff, data handoff, access & compliance checklist.
- Weeks 1–2: Build test harness, run initial tuning passes.
- Week 3: Run evaluation sweeps and hand off results + recommendations.

Owners
- Redwood AE / program lead: me (Karthik).
- Redwood SE: Marissa (cc’d) will own model config & evaluation harness.
- Engineering point: Dev Patel (for any instrumentation access/config).
- LinguaHealth: Elena for product, Samir for ML/ops, procure for contracting.

Model recommendation (initial):
- Primary: Mistral-7B-instruct (8-bit quantized) — chosen for lower latency and strong multilingual instruction tuning at small-medium sizes.
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B-chat (q4) — used for higher-quality English/complex completions when latency budget allows.

Attachments: POA_LinguaHealth_template.docx (for signature), poc_eval_prompts.csv (sample prompt set), cost_latency_estimate.xlsx (approx).

Questions / asks for LinguaHealth:
1) Can you confirm the languages to include (we propose EN, ES, PT, FR)?
2) Who from your side will own the dataset/label access for the evaluation?
3) Any minimum compliance docs we should expect before we provision dedicated trial capacity?

If this looks right I’ll send a calendar invite for a 30–45 minute kickoff (target Mon 11/9) and loop in SRE for provisioning.

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Languages: confirm EN, ES (Latin America), PT-BR, FR (EU). We may add DE later but not for the initial POC.
2) Owners: I (Elena) will own product-side evaluation and provide the labeled intent set by EOD 11/6. Samir will coordinate with our ML infra for logs and resource access. Procure asked to be copied for the POA.
3) Success criteria: the accuracy threshold looks fine, but can you add an explicit false-positive rate cap for a high-risk intent ("escalate_to_human")? We’d like FPR < 5% there.
4) Compliance: we need a brief note on how you’ll handle redaction and audit logs — SOC2 evidence is fine, but for the POC we need confirmation that logs can be retained in our customer-controlled S3 (temporary bucket) and that we can strip PHI before sending (we will pre-redact).

Please also clarify whether the latency targets are measured end-to-end (client -> Redwood -> model -> client) or server-side only.

Hi Elena / team —

Thanks — quick technical reply and an explicit POC plan draft. Addressing Elena’s questions inline and adding what we will deliver: 

1) Latency measurement: Redwood will provide both server-side generation latency (time spent on our inference runtime) and an end-to-end sample (client -> our edge -> model -> response) using your network sample. For contractable SLOs we typically measure server-side, but for the POC we will report both so you can see the variance.

2) Compliance & logs: we can write logs to a customer-controlled S3 bucket during the POC. We will provide a small audit manifest for each request and will not persist raw text in our control plane (we will redact fields flagged by you). We are happy to sign an NDA addendum or a short POA for temporary provisioning.

POC Technical Plan (deliverables)
- Day 0 (kickoff): access guide, S3 write creds test, and redaction checklist.
- Days 1–5: Ingest prompt set, run baseline using Mistral-7B-instruct (q8) and Llama-2-13B-chat (q4) to create a baseline matrix.
- Days 6–10: Prompt tuning + constrained decoding experiments for multilingual prompts; run 3 tuning passes.
- Days 11–14: Final evaluation, produce metrics dashboard and top-line recommendation.

Model notes and why this pairing: 
- Primary (Mistral-7B-instruct q8): expected to give the best latency/throughput tradeoff when quantized; good instruction-following for short Q/A style responses you described.
- Fallback (Llama-2-13B-chat q4): when quality under the primary is below threshold for certain intents (complex follow-ups or long-context replies), we’ll route those requests to the larger model as a conditional fallback. Redwood supports smart routing and automatic KV cache sharing for short-lived sessions so the switch is transparent.

Evaluation matrix (what we will report)
- Intent accuracy / class-wise breakdown (per-language).
- Answer utility: human rating (1–5) sample, and automated overlap metrics.
- Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), token counts per reply, and per-token cost estimate.
- FPR for high-risk intents ("escalate_to_human") — we will slice this specifically and include a dashboard.

Instrumentation & ownership
- Redwood SE (Marissa): evaluation harness, model config, tuning experiments.
- Redwood Eng (Dev Patel): S3 writes, temporary routing policies, and any instrumentation required in your test harness.
- LinguaHealth (Elena / Samir): labeled intent set, spot checks, and final sign-off on metrics.

Deliverables by Day 14: report (PDF), raw metrics CSV, a short recording of the demo, and a recommended model + routing policy.

I attached an updated poc_eval_prompts.csv (sample) and a quick cost/latency estimate workbook. Happy to sync tomorrow for 20 minutes if you want a deeper walkthrough of the harness.

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
